A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Private Statistical Estimation via Truncation. Their complete main text, equations, pseudocode, and Appendices A–C are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, including Gaussian estimation applications. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Its additions are explanatory remarks and a reference, without original empirical results in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: The truncation and DP-SGD procedure, recursive warm start, bounding-box algorithm, and Gaussian preconditioning remain unchanged. Algorithms 3.1, B.1, B.2, and C.1 retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios for training or evaluation. Exponential-family estimation and Gaussian mean and covariance estimation remain theoretical applications.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines. The newly cited Feldman, Koren, and Talwar work is discussed as theoretical context, without a comparison experiment.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. The algorithmic sample requirements and iteration counts are unchanged; no experimental splits, metrics, budgets, or testing procedures are introduced.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. Remark 3.2 on handling previously truncated samples is retained, merely moving across a page boundary.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical probability guarantees and boosting argument in Appendix B.5 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are present in either version. The stated estimation guarantees and sample-complexity expressions are unchanged; the added discussion does not report new measured outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, theorem and lemma statements, mathematical definitions, and proofs in Appendices A–C are unchanged. The new applicability and conditioning remarks explain scope and existing bounds without supplying revised formal results or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1, and conclusion retain the same contributions: efficient private estimation of unbounded high-dimensional exponential families, near-optimal Gaussian estimation, and improved uniform convergence guarantees.

C2.justification: A new Section 2.3 footnote describes applicability beyond absolutely continuous distributions when the empirical log-likelihood is almost surely differentiable. After Theorem 3.1, v2 explains the anti-concentration basis of the exponential conditioning dependence and weakens 'polynomial dependence' being necessary to 'some dependence.' After Theorem 3.4, it explains why potentially ill-conditioned objectives limit using sharper cited optimization bounds.

D1.justification: The pseudocode and technical instructions for projection, sampling, moment matching, and preconditioning are unchanged. No implementation settings, hardware information, or code and data access disclosures are added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Feldman, Koren, and Talwar's Private stochastic convex optimization: optimal rates in linear time [FKT20]. The discussion after Theorem 3.4 relates its sharper convergence rates to additional conditioning assumptions. The remaining research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a footnote and short explanatory passages, makes a punctuation correction, and renames 'Computational Tasks' to 'Computational Subroutines' in Section 2.3 and Appendices C.1 and C.3. Section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation spacing, footnote placement, and page breaks change locally. Theorem 3.4 becomes contained on one page, while Theorem 4.2 becomes split across pages. The same four algorithm displays remain, with no added figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision and interpretability by explaining the conditioning dependence, qualifying its necessity, and contextualizing the optimization bound through [FKT20]. These address explanatory gaps in v1 while preserving the algorithms and proofs. The minor pagination tradeoffs do not outweigh these limited benefits.
